title: Beyond Accuracy: Information-Theoretic Decoder Evaluation Under Latent Intent
abstract: arXiv:2611.05658v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A central challenge in assistive brain-to-robot control is decoding a user's latent intent from complex and noisy brain signals. Prior approaches evaluate decoders as single-trial classifiers with accuracy-based metrics, but this neglects the inherently sequential nature of assistive control. Since a planner must integrate intermittent, noisy decoder outputs over time, single-step accuracy can only be a proxy when predicting downstream task performance. We formalize brain-to-robot control as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), and prove that there is a sharp phase transition: regret is uniformly bounded across the horizon as long as pairs of goals are all decoder-distinguishable, but grows linearly otherwise. We show that a single channel statistic, the worst-pair Chernoff information $\Gamma_{\min}$ sets this boundary. tldr: 该论文将脑-机器人控制形式化为POMDP，证明了解码器性能存在由最差目标对切诺夫信息$\Gamma_{\min}$决定的相变边界——所有目标对可区分时遗憾值一致有界，否则线性增长，并据此提出闭式遗憾预测器，超越了传统的单步准确率评估指标。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes brain-to-robot control as a POMDP, proving a sharp phase transition where regret is uniformly bounded only when all goal pairs are decoder-distinguishable—as characterized by the worst-pair Chernoff information $\Gamma_{\min}$—and derives a closed-form regret predictor that supersedes single-trial accuracy metrics.
